second_derivative_test_analyticAt.text: Theorem 3.1 and the Lean statement have the same hypotheses and the same conclusion: a finite-dimensional real inner product space, a function analytic at the point, zero gradient there, a positive definite second derivative there, and a local minimum with a weak inequality on a neighbourhood. In the Lean the second derivative enters as the quadratic map sending y to its value at (y, y).

couplingPotential_analyticAt.text: Both say that the potential is analytic at every point of the plane.

couplingPotential_hasFDerivAt.text: Both give the derivative at every point x as the linear map with coefficients 2x₀ + x₁ and x₀ + 2x₁. The Lean writes it as a combination of the two coordinate projections.

couplingPotential_gradient_zero.text: Both say that the gradient of the potential at the origin is zero.

couplingPotential_iteratedFDeriv_two.text: Both give the same formula for the second derivative at every point z and every pair of vectors a and b.

couplingPotential_posDef.text: Both say that the second derivative at the origin is positive definite. The page also notes that the second derivative is the same at every point and gives the bound D²U(0)(y, y) ≥ ‖y‖²; the Lean statement is about positive definiteness at the origin only.

coupled_spring_potential.text: Theorem 5.1 and the Lean statement both say that the potential has a local minimum at the origin, with a weak inequality on a neighbourhood. Proposition 5.2 says more, a strict inequality at every other point of the plane. It is not in the author's files. The two Lean files written for this page and shown under it prove its parts.
